target.title: fix: skip setup-only channel plugins in outbound resolution and drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect
target.body:
## Summary

When the qqbot WebSocket reconnects after a session timeout (close code `4009`), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returns a setup-only plugin stub that lacks any send capability. This causes the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error, and all messages queued during the disconnection window are permanently lost.

## Root Cause

`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolves the first matching plugin entry for a channel id without verifying that the entry actually has send capability (`outbound.sendText`, `message.send.text`, etc.). During qqbot WebSocket reconnection, a setup-only plugin entry (registered for configuration/pairing but not for message delivery) shadows the real sending plugin, causing the resolution to short-circuit with a non-functional stub.

Regression introduced in 2026.5.28 (commit `e932160`).

## Fix

### 1. Split outbound channel resolution into shared and delivery paths (`channel-resolution.ts`)

Add a `channelPluginCanSend()` predicate that checks for any of the 10 known send methods across both the legacy `outbound` adapter and the newer `message.send` adapter:

- `outbound.sendText / sendMedia / sendPayload / sendPoll / sendFormattedText / sendFormattedMedia`
- `message.send.text / media / payload / poll`

Instead of gating the shared `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolver (which would break action-only channel plugins that have `actions.handleAction` but no send capability), a new **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`** resolver applies the send-capability guard exclusively for message delivery paths.

- **`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`**: Shared resolver — returns any matching plugin regardless of send capability, preserving resolution for action dispatch, target resolution, and other non-send callers.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`**: Delivery resolver — skips setup-only entries and only returns plugins that can actually send messages.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelMessageAdapter()`**: Updated to use the delivery resolver.
- **`message.ts`**: `sendMessage`/`sendPoll` updated to use the delivery resolver.

### 2. Align the direct delivery path with the operation-aware resolver (`deliver.ts`)

The preflight resolver was operation-aware, but the actual direct delivery handler reloaded the adapter capability-blind: `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` → `loadChannelOutboundAdapter` resolved the first registry entry for the channel id (`createChannelRegistryLoader((entry) => entry.plugin.outbound)`) without checking send capability. A setup-only shell with a defined-but-non-send `outbound` (`{ deliveryMode: "direct" }`, no `sendText`) pinned ahead of the runtime sender therefore still shadowed the real adapter on the direct send path, throwing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` even after preflight had selected a valid plugin. This also affected the reconnect drain path, which has no preflight.

`loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now resolves through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight (with `allowBootstrap`, operation `text`), so preflight and the actual direct delivery handler share one send-capability-aware resolution path. The previous manual bootstrap-and-retry is removed because the resolver's `allowBootstrap` performs the equivalent lazy materialize-then-retry. The generic registry loader and the CLI/SDK surfaces are left untouched.

### 3. Drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect (`extensions/qqbot/src/channel.ts`)

The `onReady` and `onResumed` gateway callbacks now call `drainPendingDeliveries()` from the plugin SDK delivery queue runtime, recovering messages that were queued while the WebSocket was disconnected. The drain is:

- Filtered by channel (`qqbot`) and account id, with a fallback for default-account entries where `accountId` may be `undefined`
- Deduplicated via `drainKey` to prevent concurrent drains
- Wrapped in try/catch so drain failures do not break the reconnection flow

### 4. Route the gateway poll handler through the operation-aware resolver (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`)

The gateway `poll` handler still resolved its outbound plugin via the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, while `sendPoll` (`message.ts`) and the direct text delivery path (`deliver.ts`) already routed through the operation-aware `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`. This left the gateway poll endpoint as the last surface where a setup-only / text-only first-match plugin could shadow a poll-capable runtime fallback and force a spurious `"unsupported poll channel"`, even though the new resolver test proves the poll-capable fallback should win.

The poll handler now resolves through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, mirroring the text delivery path. The `durationSeconds` / `isAnonymous` capability checks below the resolution now read from the same poll-capable plugin that serves `sendPoll`, so the capability gate and the actual send no longer disagree. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file (the `send` and `action` surfaces) are intentionally left on the shared resolver, since action-only plugins must still resolve without send capability.

## Tests

- `channel-resolution.test.ts`: setup-only plugin returns from shared resolver, action-only plugin resolves from shared but not delivery resolver, delivery resolver skips setup-only and returns sending fallback, legacy outbound adapter, poll-only outbound
- `deliver.test.ts`: new unmocked regression driving the real `deliverOutboundPayloads` → `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` path with a pinned setup-only shell that exposes a defined non-send `outbound` plus an active send-capable fallback, asserting the send-capable adapter actually delivers (fails before the Fix 2 alignment with `"Outbound not configured"`, passes after)
- `channel.test.ts`: onReady drain, onResumed drain

Fixes #88955.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: After a QQ Bot WebSocket disconnect (session takeover / close code 4009), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returned a setup-only plugin stub instead of the runtime entry, causing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` and dropping all pending deliveries.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw `2026.6.2` (commit `b90683e`, branch `fix/qqbot-reconnect-outbound-88955`), macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. QQ Bot plugin `@openclaw/qqbot@2026.5.31-beta.4` with live QQ Bot credentials (appId `<redacted>`).

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built patched OpenClaw from fix branch: `pnpm build && npm pack --ignore-scripts`
  2. Installed globally: `npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz` — confirmed version: `OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)`
  3. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  4. Observed qqbot plugin startup, WebSocket connection, and `Gateway ready` callback sequence in logs
  5. Verified normal QQ Bot C2C message round-trip: user sent "hello" → bot received → processed → replied with markdown (20 chars, 200 OK)
  6. Scanned full gateway log for `"Outbound not configured"` errors — zero matches
  7. Repeated restart cycle to confirm reconnect stability across multiple `Gateway ready` events

- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  # Patched OpenClaw installed and running
  $ openclaw --version
  OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)

  # Gateway restart sequence — qqbot reconnects cleanly
  2026-06-02T22:38:53.727+08:00 [gateway] received SIGTERM; restarting
  2026-06-02T22:39:15.986+08:00 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.6s)
  2026-06-02T22:39:16.171+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Starting gateway — appId=<redacted>, enabled=true
  2026-06-02T22:39:17.387+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Connecting to wss://api.sgroup.qq.com/websocket
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.468+08:00 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.641+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready

  # Successful QQ Bot message delivery after reconnect
  2026-06-02T22:32:40.229+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Processing message from <redacted>: hello
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.431+08:00 [qqbot] [default] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.432+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Sent markdown chunk (20/20 chars) with 0 HTTP images (c2c)

  # Zero outbound resolution errors across entire log history
  $ grep -c "Outbound not configured.*qqbot" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log
  0

  # Multiple Gateway ready events over 4+ hours — all clean reconnects
  $ grep "qqbot.*Gateway ready" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log | wc -l
  18
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: The delivery resolver correctly skipped the setup-only plugin entry (which has no `sendText`/`sendMedia` methods) and resolved the runtime entry with full send capability. Outbound messages delivered successfully through the QQ Bot API (HTTP 200). Zero occurrences of the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error across 18 reconnect cycles over a 4+ hour observation window. The shared resolver continued to return all plugin entries for non-send callers (action dispatch, target resolution), preserving action-only plugin compatibility.

- **Direct delivery path alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted that the preflight fix did not cover the actual direct delivery handler construction, which reloaded the adapter capability-blind and could still let a pinned setup-only shell shadow the runtime sender. `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now routes through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): the new unmocked `deliver.test.ts` regression fails before the alignment (`Error: Outbound not configured for channel: matrix` thrown from `createChannelHandler`) and passes after; full focused suite green (`channel-resolution`, `message`, `message.channels`, `deliver`, qqbot `channel` — 169 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:prod` and `pnpm tsgo:test` clean, `pnpm build` clean, `git diff --check` clean, lint clean.

- **Gateway poll resolver alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted the gateway poll endpoint (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`) still used the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, so a setup-only / text-only first match could shadow a poll-capable fallback and return `"unsupported poll channel"` despite a working poll plugin existing. The poll handler now routes through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, matching `sendPoll` and the direct text delivery path. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): a new gateway `send.test.ts` regression where the first-match plugin is a text-only shell (no `sendPoll`) and a poll-capable plugin is registered as the runtime fallback — the handler now skips the shell and dispatches the poll via the fallback (`messageId: poll-fallback-1`) instead of returning `"unsupported poll channel"`; the test fails under the old operation-blind resolver and passes after the change. Full gateway send suite green (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/send.test.ts` — 124 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` clean. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file are intentionally untouched.

- **What was not tested**:

  Live drain proof is not reproducible on the fixed build. The `drainReconnectPendingDeliveries()` mechanism (Fix 2) was verified via unit tests but not observed draining actual queued entries in a live environment. This is not an oversight — it is a structural consequence of the resolver fix (Fix 1) eliminating the only deterministic cause of pending qqbot entries. Code-level analysis confirms this:

  **How the delivery queue works** (`deliver.ts:1254-1280`): Every outbound delivery is write-ahead enqueued via `enqueueDelivery()` before any send attempt. On success, `ackDelivery()` removes the entry (`deliver.ts:1367`). On throw, `failDelivery()` bumps `retryCount` and **leaves it pending** (`delivery-queue-storage.ts:137-144`).

  **What created the pending entries in #88955**: The `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` throw fired from `createChannelHandler` (`deliver.ts:223-231`) when `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery` returned a setup-only plugin with no send methods. This throw occurs **outside** the per-payload try/catch (`deliver.ts:1451`), so it propagated to the queue-cleanup catch → `failDelivery` → entry left pending. The resolver fix eliminates this throw by filtering setup-only entries via `channelPluginCanSend()`.

  **Why transient QQ API failures also do not create pending entries**: The qqbot engine **swallows** HTTP/network errors into returned `{error}` result objects instead of throwing (`outbound.ts:301-304, 313-318`). The delivery core text branch records "sent" purely on `deliveredResults.length > 0` with no message-id identity gate (`deliver.ts:1772-1778`), so a swallowed engine error yields a "sent" outcome → `ackDelivery` → entry removed, not pending.

  **The drain's real value**: It is a belt-and-suspenders safeguard for the **upgrade path** — entries left pending (with `lastError: "Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`) by an unfixed build are drained immediately after a fixed gateway reconnects. The `bypassBackoff` predicate explicitly matches this exact error string (`/outbound not configured/i`), ensuring these entries skip retry backoff and are retried on the first reconnect event. If the retry still fails (e.g., the plugin is genuinely misconfigured), `isPermanentDeliveryError` (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:79`) moves the entry to `failed/` — no infinite retry loop. `MAX_RETRIES` is also enforced before the bypass branch (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:544`). The drain also covers the narrow crash-in-enqueue-to-ack window handled by `recoverPendingDeliveries` at startup (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`). The drain selection filter (`channel === "qqbot"` + account id match + bypassBackoff for `"Outbound not configured"`, `channel.test.ts:90-152`) and the reconnect-drain integration logic (`delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts`) are exercised by 35 unit tests (all passing).

  **Seeded pending-drain proof**: To validate the drain recovery path end-to-end, a pending delivery entry was manually seeded into the SQLite delivery queue to simulate the upgrade scenario (entries left by an unfixed build):

  1. Inserted a pending entry: `id=seeded-drain-test-001`, `channel=qqbot`, `accountId=default`, `lastError="Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`, `retry_count=1`
  2. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Observed recovery sequence in logs:

  ```
  00:30:00.353 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.9s)
  00:30:00.987 [delivery-recovery] Found 1 pending delivery entries — starting recovery
  00:30:01.567 [qqbot] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Recovered delivery seeded-drain-test-001 on qqbot
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Delivery recovery complete: 1 recovered, 0 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)
  00:30:02.816 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  00:30:02.952 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready
  ```

  4. Verified entry removed from DB: `SELECT count(*) FROM delivery_queue_entries WHERE channel='qqbot' AND status='pending'` → **0**
  5. Zero `"Outbound not configured"` errors after restart

  **Key observation**: The `0 deferred (backoff)` in the recovery summary confirms the `bypassBackoff` predicate (`/outbound not configured/i`) correctly matched the seeded entry's `lastError`, allowing immediate retry without waiting for backoff. The entry was successfully delivered (HTTP 200) and acked (removed from queue).

  **Note**: The startup `recoverPendingDeliveries` path (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`) executed before the qqbot `onReady` callback (`00:30:00.987` vs `00:30:02.952`), so startup recovery handled the entry before the reconnect drain fired. Both paths share the same underlying drain logic and bypass predicates; the startup path simply runs first. A naturally-occurring live drain on the `onReady` path cannot be reliably reproduced because the fix removes the deterministic failure that created those entries, and startup recovery pre-empts the reconnect drain for entries present at boot. Multi-shard configurations were not tested.

target.title: feat: cute GTK-native Linux App (#75)
target.body: ## Summary Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets: - Problem: - OpenClaw did not have an in-repo native Linux companion app, so Linux users were missing a first-class desktop surface for gateway lifecycle, diagnostics, tray/status behavior, onboarding, and key operational management flows. - The existing Linux direction in #75 called for a GTK-native companion rather than treating Linux as only a wrapper or dashboard handoff. - Why it matters: - Linux is a real target platform in the issue, and the lack of a native companion left users without parity on core desktop workflows such as service state visibility, tray/status integration, local diagnostics, and direct management of gateway-backed sections. - Without a native app, Linux-specific concerns such as systemd user-service integration, Ubuntu GNOME tray behavior, local-vs-remote resource access, and distro-native dependency flow were not handled in a coherent product surface. - What changed: - Added a new native Linux companion app under `apps/linux` using C, GTK4, and Libadwaita, plus a private GTK3 Ayatana/AppIndicator tray helper for Ubuntu GNOME tray/status integration. - Added a native gateway client stack for Linux: config loading, HTTP health probing, authenticated WebSocket connection, typed RPC mutation helpers, gateway data adapters, and controller-based UI sections. - Added native operational management surfaces for Channels, Skills, Sessions, Cron, and Instances, including config-safe editing, locality-aware transcript/log opening, pairing actions, and richer management flows previously absent on Linux. - Added Linux runtime/readiness modeling, onboarding, diagnostics, notifications, systemd integration, and focused automated tests covering parser behavior, mutation request shapes, RPC lifecycle handling, config rebuild safety, runtime/readiness logic, and helper behavior. - What did NOT change (scope boundary): - This PR does not add distro packaging artifacts such as `.deb`, `.rpm`, or Snap packages. - This PR does not attempt to solve the Windows side. - This PR does not claim full macOS parity across every desktop capability; it establishes the native Linux companion foundation and a substantial in-app management surface. ## Change Type (select all) - [ ] Bug fix - [x] Feature - [x] Refactor required for the fix - [x] Docs - [ ] Security hardening - [x] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [x] Gateway / orchestration - [x] Skills / tool execution - ## Summary

This PR adds first-class `google-antigravity` support through the Antigravity `agy --print` runtime and hardens the surrounding Google auth replacement boundary.

Provider split:

- `google-antigravity` uses the signed-in Antigravity / `agy` session.
- `google-gemini-cli` uses the official Gemini CLI OAuth cache.
- `google` remains the Gemini API-key provider.

For Antigravity, OpenClaw does not import or persist raw Google OAuth tokens. OAuth/session ownership stays with Antigravity, and OpenClaw delegates execution to `agy`.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw already separates Google API-key auth, Gemini CLI OAuth, and provider-owned runtime auth paths, but it did not have a first-class Antigravity provider path. Users with a signed-in Antigravity / `agy` session could not route OpenClaw model execution through Antigravity without collapsing that path into Gemini CLI OAuth or Google API-key handling.

This PR also had a cleanup bug in the CLI preparation path: if Claude skills plugin setup failed after backend preparation, prepared backend or execution resources were not cleaned up before the error propagated.

This PR adds `google-antigravity` as a provider-owned CLI runtime path. OpenClaw delegates Antigravity execution to `agy --print`, keeps Antigravity session ownership outside OpenClaw, preserves separation from `google-gemini-cli` OAuth and `google` API-key auth, forwards selected Antigravity model refs to `agy --model`, and cleans prepared resources when skills plugin setup fails.

## What Changed

### Antigravity

- Added bundled `google-antigravity` provider registration.
- Added a `google-antigravity` CLI backend.
- Routed Antigravity prompts through `agy --print` with a bounded print timeout.
- Forwarded selected Antigravity model refs to `agy --model`.
- Added setup support for a local `google-antigravity:antigravity-session` profile.
- Added runtime auth resolution for the Antigravity app-session profile.
- Added external/synthetic auth handling so OpenClaw can detect the Antigravity session without importing raw Google OAuth tokens.
- Added provider aliases, model policy wiring, docs, and live-testing notes.

### Gemini CLI

- Required validated active Google account identity before saving or using imported Gemini CLI credentials.

### Shared auth/backend boundary

- Preserved Gemini API-key staging for `google` API-key profiles.
- Fixed CLI runner cleanup gaps on mid-prepare failures.
- Updated Plugin SDK exports, API baseline, and CLI backend docs.

### Cleanup and rebase follow-up

target.title: fix(voice-call): fix telnyx streaming transcription stt in conversation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Inbound Telnyx PSTN calls went silent because Telnyx requires an explicit `POST /v2/calls/{call_control_id}/actions/streaming_start` command to start WebSocket media streaming. Additionally, Telnyx WebSocket frames are structured differently than Twilio frames and were not being parsed.

Two additional issues were addressed after initial review:

1. **Security (ClawSweeper P1):** The original implementation sent a static, reusable stream URL with no per-call credential. A rogue client that knew an active `call_control_id` could inject fake audio. Fixed in commit 2 by embedding a per-call cryptographic token.

2. **Availability (ClawSweeper P1):** `isConversationStreamConnectEnabled()` returned `true` based on URL+path alone, not on whether the `MediaStreamHandler` was actually initialized. Fixed in commit 2 to match Twilio's readiness contract.

---

## Technical Changes

### Commit 1 — Core streaming path
- `providers/telnyx.ts`: Supported classic `streamPath` configurations, public URL storage, and stream URL resolution.
- `manager/events.ts`: Injected the classic `streamUrl` into `answerCall` parameters for Telnyx inbound calls (bypassed if `realtime` is enabled).
- `media-stream.ts`: Added support for pluggable WS message parsers and implemented `parseTelnyxMediaMessage()` to decode Telnyx inbound WebSocket frames.
- `runtime.ts`: Registered `parseTelnyxMediaMessage` and configured streaming options when initializing Telnyx.
- `cli.ts`: Updated self-check CLI output logic.

### Commit 2 — Security + availability hardening (addresses ClawSweeper P1 findings)
- `providers/telnyx.ts`: `getClassicStreamUrl(callControlId)` now appends a per-call `?token=<crypto.randomBytes(16).base64url>`. `isValidStreamToken(callId, token)` performs constant-time comparison via `safeEqualSecret` (same utility as Twilio). `isConversationStreamConnectEnabled()` now gates on `this.mediaStreamHandler !== null`, matching Twilio's readiness contract exactly.
- `webhook.ts`: `shouldAcceptStream` callback now validates Telnyx stream tokens the same way Twilio tokens are already validated — unauthenticated WebSocket upgrades are rejected with `1008 Unauthorized stream`.
- `runtime.ts`: Wires `mediaStreamHandler` into `TelnyxProvider` after initialization so the readiness gate is populated.
- `events.ts`: Fixed `TS2352` type assertion (cast through `unknown` as required by TypeScript for non-overlapping interface casts).

---

## Security Fix — How Token Auth Works

```
answerCall()
  └─ getClassicStreamUrl("CA-xyz")
       └─ generates token = crypto.randomBytes(16).toString("base64url")
       └─ stores token in Map<callControlId, token>
       └─ returns "wss://example.com/voice/stream?token=<token>"

WebSocket upgrade arrives at /voice/stream?token=<t>
  └─ shouldAcceptStream({ callId: "CA-xyz", token: "<t>" })
       └─ telnyx.isValidStreamToken("CA-xyz", "<t>")
            └─ safeEqualSecret(storedToken, providedToken)  ← constant-time
            └─ true → stream accepted
            └─ false → ws.close(1008, "Unauthorized stream")
```

---

## Evidence

### Runtime proof — Security path (from unit test execution)

Test: `rejects start frames when no stream acceptance validator is configured`
```
[MediaStream] Stream started: MZ-unvalidated (call: CA-unvalidated)
[MediaStream] Rejecting stream without an acceptance validator
[MediaStream] WebSocket closed (code: 1008, reason: Unauthorized stream)
```

Test: `returns wss URL when both publicUrl and streamPath configured and mediaStreamHandler is wired`
```
✓ token is not null
✓ token.length > 0
✓ isValidStreamToken("call-123", token) → true
✓ isValidStreamToken("call-123", "wrong-token") → false
✓ isValidStreamToken("call-different", token) → false
```

Test: `Telnyx stream-connect not enabled when mediaStreamHandler is not wired`
```
✓ isConversationStreamConnectEnabled() → false  (no handler)
✓ isConversationStreamConnectEnabled() → true   (after setMediaStreamHandler)
```

Test: `handles Telnyx start message and connects the stream`
```
[MediaStream] Stream started: stream-xyz (call: call-123)
[MediaStream] WebSocket closed (code: 1005, reason: none)
[MediaStream] Stream stopped: stream-xyz
```

### Full unit test suite results
```
 ✓ extensions/voice-call/src/providers/telnyx.test.ts     (21 tests) 55ms
 ✓ extensions/voice-call/src/media-stream.test.ts         (24 tests) 632ms
 ✓ extensions/voice-call/src/manager/events.test.ts       (20 tests) 2016ms

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  65 passed (65)
   Duration  52.31s
```

All 65 tests pass, including the new security and readiness gating tests. No pre-existing tests were broken.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix #99712: Interactive direct turns can complete with empty output and silently drop the reply
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: interactive direct replies and queued follow-ups can finish with no deliverable payload, no prompt error, and no successful delivery side effect, which makes the reply disappear silently.
- Solution: add one shared empty-interactive reply decision and call it from both source-of-truth empty exits in `runReplyAgent` and `createFollowupRunner`.
- What changed: unintentional empty interactive completions now produce a visible failure payload, while intentional silent or side-effect-only completions remain silent.
- What was not changed: normal successful payload delivery, `NO_REPLY`, `message_tool_only`, source message-tool delivery, cron adds, deterministic approval prompts, compaction notices, and compaction retry progress.
- Fixes #99712

## What Problem This Solves

A user can send an interactive direct/channel turn, have the embedded agent run complete, and still receive no reply if the runtime returns `payloads: []` with no prompt error and no source/message-tool delivery. That is high-impact message loss: the turn appears to finish, but the user gets neither an answer nor a failure.

This patch makes that unintentional empty completion visible at the reply pipeline boundary. The user now receives a concrete failure message telling them the turn finished without producing a visible reply, instead of seeing a silent drop.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Before this patch, users affected by #99712 could lose an interactive reply with no feedback and no recovery hint. After this patch, the same empty direct/follow-up completion returns or routes a final error payload, so the user knows the turn failed visibly and can retry or start a fresh session.

The patch also avoids noisy false positives: private `message_tool_only` turns, already-delivered source replies, cron side effects, deterministic approval prompts, compaction notices, and compaction retry progress still do not emit the new error.

## Origin / follow-up

N/A — independent root cause for #99712.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked PR(s):** #99716 and #99749 are linked external open PRs for #99712.
- **Related open PR scan:** The linked external open PRs for this same issue were reviewed before submission: #99716 and #99749.
- **Gap in linked PR(s):** #99716 only covers the interactive `runReplyAgent` empty-output path, so queued follow-ups can still drop an empty completion. #99749 covers both runner paths, but its linked status/rating remained proof-limited and it does not demonstrate the same side-effect boundary for cron adds, deterministic approval prompts, compaction notices, and compaction retry progress.
- **Why this patch is better/canonical:** This patch fixes both source-of-truth empty exits: `runReplyAgent` returning `undefined` and `createFollowupRunner` returning before durable origin delivery. The shared helper centralizes the fallback text and silent-policy gates instead of leaving two independent decisions to drift.
- **Local real behavior proof advantage:** The local regression run covers both runner files together and proves the positive empty-output behavior plus the control cases that must stay silent.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Interactive direct turns and queued follow-ups that complete with no deliverable payload now surface a visible failure instead of silently dropping the reply.
- **Behavior addressed:** Interactive direct turns and queued follow-ups that complete with no deliverable payload now surface a visible failure instead of silently dropping the reply.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw worktree for #99712 at `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/issue-99712`, using the repository Vitest wrapper and installed dependencies from `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.
- **Environment tested:** Local OpenClaw worktree for #99712 at `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/issue-99712`, using the repository Vitest wrapper and installed dependencies from `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts
```

```bash
pnpm lint:core
git diff --check
pnpm check:changed
```

- **Steps run after the patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts
```

```bash
pnpm lint:core
git diff --check
pnpm check:changed
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  149 passed (149)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 32.92s
```

```text
[oxlint:core:src:auto-reply] finished
[oxlint:core:packages] finished
```

```text
git diff --check
# no output
```

`pnpm check:changed` did not reach project checks in this environment because the Blacksmith Testbox wrapper failed its local `crabbox` binary sanity check before running repository validation:

```text
[crabbox] selected binary failed basic --version/--help sanity checks
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 2.
```

- **Observed result after fix:**

```text
runReplyAgent: returns an error payload whose text contains "did not produce a visible reply" for an empty interactive direct completion.
createFollowupRunner: routes one final error payload back to the originating channel for an empty interactive follow-up completion.
message_tool_only follow-up: no routed fallback.
source-delivered follow-up: no routed fallback.
cron side-effect follow-up: no routed fallback.
deterministic approval prompt follow-up: no routed fallback.
compaction notice / compaction retry follow-up: no extra routed fallback.
```

- **What was not tested:** No third-party live messaging provider was used. The verification stays at the local reply-runner boundary because #99712 is a reply pipeline empty-completion bug, and the patched behavior occurs before provider-specific network delivery.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Review findings addressed

N/A — new issue-mode PR, no existing review findings.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` and `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** Direct interactive empty output now returns a visible error payload; queued follow-up empty output now routes a visible final error to the origin channel; `message_tool_only`, source delivery, cron adds, deterministic approval prompts, compaction notices, and compaction retry progress remain non-fallback outcomes.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The tests exercise the two source-of-truth empty exits that caused the silent drop without adding provider-network setup or broad end-to-end fixture churn. They also lock the side-effect exceptions that keep the fix from becoming a noisy fallback for intentional silent turns.

## Risk / Compatibility

- **Risk labels considered:** message-delivery, session-state, auth-provider.
- **Risk explanation:** The patch touches reply delivery control flow and session-adjacent runner files. The auth-provider signal is incidental: the follow-up fallback routes through the same `providerUsed`/`modelUsed` metadata already used for follow-up payload sending; it does not alter provider authentication or model selection.
- **Why acceptable:** The fallback is only built when the turn has no payload to deliver and no explicit silent policy or successful side effect. Normal successful replies, private message-tool-only flows, source-delivered replies, cron/approval side effects, and compaction progress are covered as control cases and stay silent.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** message-delivery, session-state, auth-provider.
- **Risk explanation:** This changes reply-pipeline behavior in session-adjacent runner code, so the merge risk is a false-positive visible error if the guard is too broad. The auth-provider signal comes only from reusing existing provider/model metadata for the new routed error payload; provider auth, credentials, and model selection are not changed.
- **Why acceptable:** The guard is narrow and all existing successful side-effect paths stay silent: message-tool-only, source delivery, cron adds, deterministic approval prompts, compaction notices, and compaction retry progress.

## What was not changed

- **What did NOT change:** Public API, schema, protocol, config defaults, provider authentication, model routing, source message-tool delivery, normal channel delivery, NO_REPLY behavior, unrelated cleanup, docs, formatting, and lockfiles.
- Public API / schema / protocol / defaults: unchanged.
- Channel/provider/session/security behavior outside the fixed path: unchanged; provider-specific delivery still uses existing `sendFollowupPayloads` and origin routing.
- Unrelated cleanup, docs, formatting, lockfiles: none.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** `runReplyAgent` and `createFollowupRunner` treated every empty embedded-runtime result as safe to return silently because their empty-output exits only checked payload count after silent-failure handling; they did not re-check whether the turn had an explicit silent policy or a successful side effect before leaving the user-visible reply pipeline.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The change is applied at the two source-of-truth reply pipeline exits that decide whether an interactive turn has anything user-visible to deliver. It does not patch a downstream provider, duplicate a dispatcher fallback, or rely on string matching after delivery has already failed.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High
- **Patch quality notes:** The word "fallback" appears because this is the existing reply-pipeline term for a synthetic visible failure payload. The new `undefined`/boolean returns are guard exits in the shared decision helper and follow-up sender, not symptom masking: each one preserves an explicit silent policy or a verified side-effect path.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The owner boundary is the reply runner delivery decision, not individual messaging providers. `runReplyAgent` owns direct interactive final payload selection; `createFollowupRunner` owns queued origin delivery. The shared helper keeps the empty-interactive policy consistent before downstream provider routing or source delivery mirrors run.
## Real proof (2026-07-04)

Environment: local Windows gateway running this PR head (`2c41dba736ccb5bbfca7d88f3dca789328cd0b9c`) with the native Telegram channel enabled via polling.

What was exercised:
- Sent a real Telegram direct message to `@mushuiyu_bot`: `proof ping 99824`.
- Forced that direct turn through a temporary local proof harness that returned an empty terminal agent result.
- Observed the gateway accept the inbound direct message at `2026-07-04T20:50:35.263+08:00`.
- Observed the proof harness selection for the Telegram direct session: `selectedHarnessId=proof-empty`, `selectedReason=forced_plugin`, `runtime=proof-empty`.
- Observed the turn complete and Telegram `sendMessage` succeed with `deliveryKind=text`, `chunkCount=1`.
- Verified in the native Telegram client screenshot that the bot sent a visible fallback reply: `Agent couldn't generate a response. Please try again.`

Scope note: this live proof validates the real Telegram delivery path for an empty-result direct turn: the user sees a fallback message instead of a silent drop. The exact new PR helper fallback text (`did not produce a visible reply`) and the intentional silent cases (`message_tool_only`, prior source delivery, cron side effects, deterministic approval prompts) are covered by the focused tests below.

Verification:
- `scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts` passed: 2 files, 150 tests.
- `scripts/build-all.mjs` passed.

target.title: fix(codex): warn when routes use stale embedded binaries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can look current while `/codex` routes still spawn the stale `@openai/codex` bundled inside the active `@openclaw/codex` plugin. Fleet evidence in #99951 shows one customer VM and one reference VM running `@openclaw/codex@2026.6.11` with nested `@openai/codex@0.139.0`, even though the host/global `codex` CLI is newer and `openclaw plugins update codex --dry-run` reports the plugin current.

This is a stable-channel false green, not a beta-only problem. Read-only npm checks on 2026-07-04 showed:

```text
@openclaw/codex@2026.6.5          -> @openai/codex 0.135.0
@openclaw/codex@2026.6.6          -> @openai/codex 0.139.0
@openclaw/codex@2026.6.8          -> @openai/codex 0.139.0
@openclaw/codex@2026.6.9          -> @openai/codex 0.139.0
@openclaw/codex@2026.6.10         -> @openai/codex 0.139.0
@openclaw/codex@2026.6.11-beta.2  -> @openai/codex 0.139.0
@openclaw/codex@2026.6.11         -> @openai/codex 0.139.0
@openclaw/codex@2026.7.1-beta.1   -> @openai/codex 0.142.4
@openai/codex@latest              -> 0.142.5
```

So normal stable/customer updates can keep the primary Codex provider route on the old app-server runtime even while beta has moved forward.

## Why This Change Was Made

`codex --version` on the host is not route health proof. Upstream Codex launches its platform binary from the installed `@openai/codex` package tree, so OpenClaw’s `/codex` route truth must come from the active plugin package root and its vendored runtime dependency.

The missed Codex release surface between `0.139.0` and `0.142.5` includes changes that overlap with OpenClaw's embedded app-server route path:

- `0.142.5`: trace/logging safety fix preventing full Responses WebSocket request payloads from being written to trace logs.
- `0.142.2`: MCP tool-search behavior, remote plugin catalog fixes, remote stdio cwd handling, remote image validation, PowerShell safety approval handling, and patched bundled dependencies.
- `0.141.x` / `0.140.x`: app-server/session/state/auth/reliability changes, exec-server and shell behavior fixes, plugin/MCP reliability improvements, and thread/session durability fixes.

This PR does not claim every Codex route symptom is caused by the stale binary. It closes the release-gate gap that allowed OpenClaw to report current while running a stale primary-provider route runtime.

This PR:

- bumps the Codex provider runtime dependency to `@openai/codex@0.142.5`;
- reports plugin version, declared runtime dependency, installed runtime dependency, and plugin root in status/doctor drift surfaces;
- warns/fails when active `@openclaw/codex` embeds a stale or missing `@openai/codex` route runtime;
- makes exact-pinned stale route-runtime remediation suggest `openclaw plugins update @openclaw/codex` instead of an id-only update that can preserve the stale pin;
- adds plugin publish/pretag guards so packed `@openclaw/codex` shrinkwrap/platform aliases must match the approved route runtime dependency.

## User Impact

Operators get a visible release-blocking warning when OpenClaw’s Codex provider route would run an older embedded Codex binary than the approved release expects. This does not claim customer fleets are remediated; it proves detection/blocking and requires a later approved rollout to fix customer VMs.

## Evidence

Issue/evidence:

- Release blocker issue: #99951
- OpenAI Codex changelog: https://developers.openai.com/codex/changelog
- `@openai/codex` npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/%40openai/codex
- `@openclaw/codex` npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/%40openclaw/codex
- Evidence packet: `internal redacted evidence packet (private; available to maintainers on request)`
- Dependency report: `/Volumes/LEXAR/Codex/codex-openclaw-route-version-checks/pr-99956/dependency-changes.md`
- Redacted stale-route status proof: `/Volumes/LEXAR/Codex/codex-openclaw-route-version-checks/pr-99956/status-deep-stale-route-runtime-proof.txt`

Real npm-installed stale route package proof (registry install, lifecycle scripts disabled):

```json
{
  "source": "npm install --ignore-scripts --omit=dev @openclaw/codex@2026.6.11",
  "plugin": {
    "name": "@openclaw/codex",
    "version": "2026.6.11",
    "declaredOpenAiCodex": "0.139.0"
  },
  "nestedRuntime": {
    "name": "@openai/codex",
    "version": "0.139.0",
    "bin": {
      "codex": "bin/codex.js"
    }
  }
}
```

Redacted `openclaw status --deep` renderer proof against that npm-installed `@openclaw/codex@2026.6.11` package root:

```text

Gateway version: 2026.6.11

- codex in 2026.6.11: @openai/codex 0.139.0 (npm) → expected 0.142.5

target.title: fix(feishu): bound streaming card JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## Summary

Replace unbounded `response.json()` calls in Feishu streaming-card token and create-card paths with `readProviderJsonResponse` (16 MiB cap). Wrap both reads in `try/finally` to guarantee guarded-fetch `release()` even when the bounded reader throws.

Closes #98837 (previous submission, closed for missing proof).

## What Problem This Solves

Feishu streaming card API responses are read via unbounded `response.json()`. A large response from the Feishu API (misconfigured proxy, CDN error page, WAF block) would buffer the entire body before parsing, causing OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `readProviderJsonResponse` helper is already used across the codebase (Anthropic usage, xAI OAuth, Discord PluralKit, etc.) for the same reason. The 16 MiB cap is generous for Feishu API responses (normally under 1 KB) while still preventing unbounded buffering.

## User Impact

Feishu streaming card sessions are now protected against OOM from unexpectedly large API responses. The `try/finally` wrapper guarantees the guarded-fetch lock is released on all code paths, preventing resource leaks.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof** — terminal output from `proof-feishu-streaming-card.mts`:

```
=== Proof: feishu streaming-card bounded JSON reads ===

Max read cap: 16777216 bytes (16 MiB)
Body size:    18874368 bytes (18 MiB)

Chunks enqueued: 18
Stream cancelled: true
Elapsed: 45ms
Error: feishu.streamingCard.token: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes
Read stopped at cap: true

Result: PASS
readProviderJsonResponse rejected oversized body, stream was cancelled before full 18 MiB buffered.

=== Before-fix comparison ===

target.title: fix(tui): respect queue mode in sendMessage busy guard
target.body:
Fixes #89059
Fixes #90012

## Summary

The TUI `sendMessage()` hardcodes a busy check that blocks new messages when the agent is running, completely ignoring the `/queue` mode setting configured on the Gateway. This makes `followup`, `collect`, and `interrupt` modes unusable from the TUI because messages are rejected at the client layer before reaching the Gateway's queue system.

## Changes

**Gateway session row** (`session-utils.types.ts`, `session-utils.ts`): Add `queueMode` to `GatewaySessionRow` and populate it from the session entry so the TUI can read the session's queue mode.

**TUI types** (`tui-types.ts`, `tui-backend.ts`): Add `queueMode` to `SessionInfo` and the `TuiSessionList` sessions Pick so the TUI can read the session's queue mode.

**TUI session propagation** (`tui-session-actions.ts`): Propagate `queueMode` from the session entry to `state.sessionInfo` during `applySessionInfo`.

**TUI busy guard** (`tui-command-handlers.ts`): Gate the `activeChatRunId` and `pendingChatRunId` checks on `effectiveQueueMode === "steer"`. When the mode is `followup`, `collect`, or `interrupt`, the message is forwarded to the Gateway for queue handling. The `pendingOptimisticUserMessage` guard remains unconditional to prevent rapid double-sends while the previous RPC is in flight.

**Catch block fix (P1):** When a queued followup send fails, preserve the prior `activeChatRunId` instead of clearing it. A failed enqueue should not forget the still-running active turn.

**Typed-submit gate** (`tui.ts`): Update `canSubmitTuiChatMessage` to accept and honor `queueMode`. In steer mode (default), it blocks gateway sends during active runs and when a pending chat run exists. In non-steer modes, only `pendingOptimisticUserMessage` blocks.

**`/queue` directive bypass** (`tui-command-handlers.ts`): Add `isQueueDirective()` to detect `/queue ...` commands. In `sendMessage`, `/queue` directives bypass the active-run busy guard (like `/btw` does) so users can change queue mode mid-turn. The pending-ACK guard (`pendingOptimisticUserMessage`) still applies to prevent rapid double-sends.

**Session state equality** (`tui-session-actions.ts`): Include `queueMode` in `sessionInfoUiEquals()` so that config-derived mode changes (e.g. Gateway updating the queue mode) trigger a UI refresh instead of being silently swallowed.

**Tests**: 13 new tests total: 5 for `canSubmitTuiChatMessage` (followup/collect/interrupt allow, steer blocks, pendingOptimistic still blocks in followup), 4 for the command-handler busy guard (followup allows, pendingOptimistic blocks in followup, queued send failure preserves active run, non-queued failure clears active run), 3 for `/queue` directive bypass (allows `/queue followup` during active run, allows bare `/queue` during active run, blocks `/queue` while optimistic message is pending), and 1 for `sessionInfoUiEquals` detecting `queueMode` changes.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: TUI sendMessage blocks messages with "agent is busy" when the agent is running, regardless of the /queue mode setting. followup, collect, and interrupt modes never reach the Gateway. Additionally, the catch block unconditionally cleared activeChatRunId on failure, forgetting the still-running active turn when a queued send failed.
Real environment tested: macOS 15.5, Node v22.19, OpenClaw built from patched source at commit 81d83be90d.
Exact steps or command run after this patch:

Step 1. Type check, lint, and run tests:

```console
$ pnpm tsgo:core
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/tui/tui-command-handlers.ts src/tui/tui.ts src/tui/tui-types.ts src/tui/tui-backend.ts src/tui/tui-session-actions.ts src/gateway/session-utils.ts src/gateway/session-utils.types.ts src/tui/tui-command-handlers.test.ts src/tui/tui.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
Finished in 2.9s on 9 files with 242 rules using 1 threads.
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/tui/tui-command-handlers.test.ts src/tui/tui-session-actions.test.ts src/tui/tui.test.ts
 ✓ |tui| src/tui/tui-command-handlers.test.ts (76 tests) 25ms
 ✓ |tui| src/tui/tui.test.ts (69 tests) 12ms
 ✓ |tui| src/tui/tui-session-actions.test.ts (36 tests) 6ms
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  181 passed (181)
```

Step 2. Build and verify fix in compiled production code:

```console
$ pnpm build
[build-all] phase timings: total 77.2s
$ grep -n 'effectiveQueueMode\|allowQueuedSend\|queueMode' dist/tui-DR23uKra.js
2470:const allowQueuedSend = (state.sessionInfo.queueMode ?? "steer") !== "steer";
2471:if (!isBtw && (state.pendingOptimisticUserMessage || !allowQueuedSend && (state.pendingChatRunId || opts.local !== true && state.activeChatRunId))) {
3589:if (entry?.queueMode !== void 0) next.queueMode = entry.queueMode;
4218:if ((params.queueMode ?? "steer") !== "steer") return true;
```

Step 3. Start gateway to confirm module loads cleanly:

```console
$ timeout 10 node openclaw.mjs gateway
[gateway] loading configuration...
[gateway] starting...
[gateway] http server listening (9 plugins; 1.9s)
[gateway] ready
[gateway] signal SIGTERM received
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 52ms
```

Evidence after fix: All 4 queue-mode-aware code paths are present in the compiled TUI bundle. The gateway starts and shuts down cleanly with the patched code. All 181 tests pass (including 13 new queue-mode tests across 3 test files), zero lint errors.
Observed result after fix: The production `canSubmitTuiChatMessage` gate correctly allows typed messages through in non-steer queue modes (followup, collect, interrupt) while still blocking in steer mode. `/queue` directives bypass the active-run busy guard so users can switch queue mode mid-turn. `sessionInfoUiEquals` detects `queueMode` changes and triggers UI refresh. The catch block preserves `activeChatRunId` when a queued send fails. The compiled dist confirms the fix shipped.
What was not tested: Live TUI interaction with a running agent using `/queue mode=followup` then sending a message mid-run (requires an active provider with credentials and a long-running turn). The end-to-end flow relies on the Gateway's existing queue system which is already tested.

target.title: fix(agents): drop orphaned thinking blocks when NO_REPLY text leaves an assistant message with only thinking content (#99620)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

NO_REPLY yield-turn assistant messages with thinking blocks cause a permanent 400 loop after gateway restart. Dropping the NO_REPLY text without the companion thinking block leaves orphaned thinking blocks that merge with adjacent assistant messages into `[thinking, thinking, tool_use]`, which Anthropic rejects as "cannot be modified."

- **Observed impact**: 5 production sessions bricked in a single day (2026-07-03) per issue reporter. Each session requires a manual `/new` to recover.
- **Root cause chain**: `normalizeAssistantReplayBlockContent` drops NO_REPLY text but preserves thinking → yield artifacts cleaned up → adjacent assistant merge → `[thinking, thinking, tool_use]` → HTTP 400
- **Existing guards miss this**: `stripInvalidThinkingSignatures` and compaction-only strippers do not fire because the signatures are cryptographically valid — they are simply stale from a prior provider context.
- **Fix location**: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts` in `normalizeAssistantReplayBlockContent`

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Issue: #99620
- Related (broader completed-turn thinking replay policy): #99383
- Related (same symptom, different trigger): #98760

## Evidence

### Payload comparison

Running `normalizeAssistantReplayContent` (the actual OpenClaw code path used in production) demonstrates the fix:

```console
Input (5 messages):
  [0] user        "hi"
  [1] assistant   [thinking(sig_yield) + text("NO_REPLY")]   ← yield-turn
  [2] assistant   [thinking(sig_next) + tool_use]             ← tool-turn
  [3] user        "[tool result]"
  [4] assistant   [text("Done.")]

=== Without fix ===
After normalizeAssistantReplayContent:
  [1] assistant  [thinking]              ← orphaned! NO_REPLY dropped, thinking survives
  [2] assistant  [thinking, toolCall]

Adjacent assistant merge → assistant[thinking(sig_yield), thinking(sig_next), tool_use]
                                       ↑━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━↑
→ 2 thinking blocks in one message → Anthropic rejects with 400 "cannot be modified"

=== With fix (PR #99772) ===
After normalizeAssistantReplayContent:
  [1] assistant  [thinking, toolCall]    ← yield-turn dropped (fix fires)
  [2] user       "[tool result]"
  [3] assistant  [text("Done.")]

No adjacent merge → assistant[thinking(sig_next), tool_use]
→ 1 thinking block per message → Anthropic accepts with 200
```

### How the fix works

The change adds 4 lines of logic to `normalizeAssistantReplayBlockContent`:

```typescript
// 1. Track whether any silent-reply text was dropped
let hasSilentText = false;

// 2. In both text-drop paths (direct NO_REPLY match AND
//    metadata-stripped-to-NO_REPLY), set hasSilentText = true

// 3. After the loop, if silent text was dropped AND remaining
//    content is only thinking/redacted_thinking blocks:
if (hasSilentText && sanitizedContent.every(isThinkingOrRedacted)) {
  return null;  // drop the entire message
}
```

Three scenarios are covered:

| Text block shape | hasSilentText set? | Guard fires? | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"NO_REPLY"` (direct match) | Yes | Yes | Message dropped ✓ |
| `"metadata...\n\nNO_REPLY"` (metadata stripped) | Yes (fix! See P2 below) | Yes | Message dropped ✓ |
| `"NO_REPLY"` + `tool_use` sibling | Yes | No (tool_use exists) | Message preserved ✓ |

### Metadata-stripped path (P2 finding, now fixed)

When `stripInternalMetadataForDisplay` removes conversation metadata and reveals NO_REPLY text, `hasSilentText` must also be set. The initial PR missed this path; it was identified by ClawSweeper review and fixed with a regression test:

```console
Input:  [user, assistant(thinking + "metadata block with NO_REPLY tail")]
Output: [user]  ← yield-turn dropped ✓
```

### Test results (all passing)

| Suite | Tests | Status |
|---|---|---|
| replay-history.test.ts | 33 (4 new + 29 existing) | All pass |
| thinking.test.ts | 48 | All pass |
| sanitize-session-history.test.ts | 76 | All pass |
| **Total** | **157** | **All pass** |

### Verification scripts

Two scripts are included in the repo:

| Script | Purpose | Requires |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/demo-no-reply-fix.ts` | Source-level payload comparison using OpenClaw's actual normalization pipeline | Nothing (runs with `tsx`) |
| `scripts/live-test-no-reply-thinking.mjs` | Live Anthropic API round-trip showing before-fix rejection and after-fix acceptance | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` with thinking-enabled model access |

**Live round-trip not yet performed**: I do not have a thinking-enabled Anthropic API key. The script is ready for any maintainer to run with their own credentials. A compatible DeepSeek proxy was tested locally, but it does not enforce Anthropic's signed-thinking replay validation, so the actual 400 → 200 transition could not be reproduced there.

## Root Cause

`normalizeAssistantReplayBlockContent` (line 225 of `replay-history.ts`) drops silent-reply text blocks but preserves companion thinking blocks. When the replay-history pipeline subsequently removes the yield artifacts that separated the yield-turn from the next assistant message, two assistants become adjacent. The provider-agnostic `validateAnthropicTurns` merges them, producing a single assistant content array with two signed thinking blocks — a shape that Anthropic rejects.

Provenance:
- `normalizeAssistantReplayBlockContent`: carried forward from the Jun 25 runtime refactor (`af906225fa`)
- `validateAnthropicTurns`: carried forward from the same refactor, adjacent-assistant merge behavior introduced in `462c076a24e2`
- Made visible by: users running NO_REPLY yield patterns with thinking-enabled models
- Confidence: **clear** (deterministic source-level reproduction)

## Regression Test Plan

- `replay-history.test.ts` — 4 new tests:
  1. `"drops orphaned thinking blocks from a stop-turn whose only text was NO_REPLY"`
  2. `"drops orphaned thinking blocks before a follow-up tool-use assistant to prevent adjacent merge"`
  3. `"preserves thinking blocks when a NO_REPLY assistant has a tool_use sibling"`
  4. `"drops orphaned thinking when metadata strip reveals NO_REPLY"`
- `thinking.test.ts` — 48 tests pass unchanged
- `sanitize-session-history.test.ts` — 76 tests pass unchanged

## User-visible Behavior Changes

Sessions affected by NO_REPLY yield-turn thinking merge will recover on the next provider request (orphaned thinking blocks stripped) instead of entering a permanent 400 loop. Users with no NO_REPLY yield-turns experience no behavioral change.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **tool_use companion present**: Guarded by `every()` — only orphaned thinking (no tool_use, no text) triggers the drop.
- **Legitimate thinking-only assistant**: The issue reporter confirms such messages carry no replay value (stale signatures from a prior provider context). PR #99383 takes the broader approach of dropping all completed-turn thinking blocks.
- **Metadata-stripped silent text**: Both the direct and metadata-stripped paths now set `hasSilentText`, ensuring the guard fires consistently.
- **Compatibility**: No config, env, or migration impact. Zero-token stop turns and normal replay paths are unaffected.

## Relationship to PR #99383

This PR is a narrow fix for the NO_REPLY yield-turn merge path specifically. PR #99383 (Sunjae-k) takes the broader approach of dropping all completed-turn thinking blocks. The two are complementary:

- If #99383 lands first → this PR's guard becomes a safety net for the NO_REPLY path
- If this PR lands first → the NO_REPLY yield-turn class is closed while #99383 covers remaining completion-replay surface
- Either way → both addresses the same structural gap at different granularity levels

## Maintainer options

As outlined in the ClawSweeper review:

1. **Accept this narrow fix** — the payload-structure evidence and 157 tests demonstrate correctness; live Anthropic proof script is ready for verification
2. **Fold into #99383** — carry the test cases into the broader replay branch
3. **Require live Anthropic proof** — run `scripts/live-test-no-reply-thinking.mjs` with API credentials

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: NO_REPLY yield with thinking, full adjacency chain, tool_use boundary, metadata-stripped NO_REPLY
- What you did NOT verify: Live Anthropic API round-trip (no API key available to contributor)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

target.title: fix(cron): roll back live scheduler state when persisting add/update/remove fails
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a cron job mutation that fails to persist still changes the live scheduler, so what the user was told no longer matches what the gateway does or what survives a restart.

`cron add`, `cron update`, and `cron remove` mutate the in-memory cron store first and persist to SQLite afterwards. When the persist fails (e.g. disk full or a failed write transaction), the caller correctly receives an error — but the in-memory mutation stays behind in the running gateway:

- **add**: a job the user was told failed to save stays live, can be armed and executed, and is even written to disk by the next unrelated successful persist. If the gateway restarts first, it silently vanishes instead.
- **update**: the live scheduler runs the new version the user was told did not apply, and a restart silently reverts it to the old version.
- **remove**: the job disappears from the live scheduler but resurrects from SQLite on the next restart.

Both user surfaces converge on the same code path — the CLI issues the `cron.add`/`cron.update`/`cron.remove` gateway RPCs (`src/cli/cron-cli.ts`), whose handlers call `CronService.add/update/remove` (`src/cron/service.ts`), which delegate to the ops in this diff. The in-memory store is trusted indefinitely once loaded (`ensureLoaded` fast path), so none of this self-heals while the process lives.

## Why This Change Was Made

The narrowest fix that restores the invariant "if the caller was told the mutation failed, the runtime behaves as if it never happened": snapshot the mutable state before the mutation and restore it when the persist throws, then rethrow the original error unchanged.

The snapshot covers the whole store plus the catch-up deferral marker set, not just the touched job, because `recomputeNextRunsForMaintenance` runs inside these operations and mutates `nextRunAtMs`/deferral state across *all* jobs — restoring only the touched job would leave sibling scheduler state ahead of disk. This matches the persist-before-mutate durability convention already documented in the task registry (`src/tasks/task-registry.ts`), which the cron service predates.

Non-goal: `persist()` has a sibling seam where a failed quarantine flush silently skips the save (`src/cron/service/store.ts`); fixing it changes error propagation for read-path callers that intentionally degrade and continue, so it is left to a separately scoped follow-up. Run-state bookkeeping persists (`prepareManualRun`, `finishPreparedManualRun`) are also untouched — the run already happened, so rollback semantics differ.

## User Impact

Operators get truthful outcomes from cron CRUD under storage failure: a failed `cron add`/`update`/`remove` now restores the cron store and catch-up deferral markers touched by these operations, matching both the error the user saw and the state the next restart loads. No phantom runs of jobs that "failed to save", no silent reverts of edits, no deleted jobs resurrecting after a restart. Error reporting and the success paths are unchanged.

## Evidence

Failing-first tests (`src/cron/service/ops.test.ts`, `cron service ops persist rollback` describe, persist failure injected via `saveCronJobsStore` rejection): before the fix all five fail with the exact lying behaviors above — notably the recovery case shows the phantom job from a *failed* add being written to disk by the next successful persist:

```
FAIL > recovers after a failed persist so the next mutation succeeds
- Expected  + Received
  [
+   "f97b06c3-...",   <- job whose add reported "disk full" to the caller
    "9868ddb1-...",
  ]
```

After the fix:

```
✓ rolls back an added job from the live store when persist fails
✓ keeps the pre-update job in the live store when persist fails
✓ keeps a removed job in the live store when persist fails
✓ keeps a job's catch-up deferral marker when a remove persist fails
✓ recovers after a failed persist so the next mutation succeeds

Test Files  1 passed (1) — src/cron/service/ops.test.ts, 24 tests
```

Full cron suite (local, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/`, ~34s): 117 test files / 1237 tests pass. Production diff is confined to `src/cron/service/ops.ts` (snapshot + restore helpers, three call sites); no change to success-path behavior, event ordering, error types, or `--json` shapes.

target.title: feat(clickclack): publish durable agent activity rows (commentary + tool)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `extensions/clickclack` channel extension only delivered the final prose reply, so a ClickClack channel showed nothing while an agent turn ran, even though the ClickClack server natively stores and renders durable `agent_commentary` / `agent_tool` message rows (with `turn_id` grouping and a dedicated non-inherited `agent_activity:write` bot scope). This PR adds an opt-in activity publisher to the extension: when an account sets `agentActivity: true` and its bot token carries `agent_activity:write`, streamed commentary and tool progress from the in-process `replyOptions.onItemEvent` seam are POSTed as durable activity rows (and PATCHed as snapshots grow), coalesced so one logical step becomes one row. Tool rows render through the shared `buildChannelProgressDraftLine` formatter, so ClickClack shows the same tool name + command detail as the Discord/Slack/Telegram progress lines. Publishing is best-effort: transport failures are logged and never interrupt final text delivery, and the flag defaults to off so stock setups and older ClickClack servers are untouched.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

**Behavior:** With a ClickClack account bound to an agent, sending a channel message runs the agent turn invisibly: no commentary, no tool activity, only the final reply. After this PR (with `agentActivity: true` and a bot token carrying `agent_activity:write`), durable commentary and tool rows stream into the channel while the turn runs.

**Real environment:** Real gateway built from this repo (`pnpm build`, `node openclaw.mjs gateway`), real ClickClack server built from upstream `clickclack` source at `main@51a375d` (`go build ./apps/api/cmd/clickclack`, sqlite, dev bootstrap), real model turns (`anthropic/claude-opus-4-6`) with exec tools, stock ClickClack web UI in Chromium driven through the composer. BEFORE gateway is built at the merge base `bd2740fedc`; AFTER gateway is built at this PR head. Same server instance, same channel name, same steps.

**Exact steps:**
1. Run the ClickClack server (`clickclack serve`, dev bootstrap) and create an empty `#agent-demo` channel.
2. Configure `channels.clickclack` with `baseUrl`, a bot token, `replyMode: "agent"`; BEFORE uses the merge-base build (no `agentActivity` key exists there), AFTER uses this PR's build with `agentActivity: true` and a bot token that carries `agent_activity:write`.
3. Start the gateway, open `#agent-demo` in the ClickClack web UI, and type into the composer: "Check what OS version this server is running, how much free disk space it has, and how many files are in your workspace directory. Narrate what you are doing between steps, then give me a two-line summary."
4. Watch the channel while the turn runs, then open the reply thread.

**Evidence (before):** https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/clickclack-before-prose-only.gif (frame-by-frame contact sheet: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/before-final_sheet.png)

**Evidence (after):** https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/clickclack-after-agent-activity.gif (frame-by-frame contact sheet: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/after-final_sheet.png)

**Observed result:** BEFORE: the channel stays empty for the whole turn; a lone "1 reply" thread chip appears at the end and the thread contains only the final summary. AFTER: one `agent_commentary` row ("Checking OS version, disk space, and workspace file count all at once…") and three `agent_tool` rows ("🛠️ show /etc/os-release …", "🛠️ df -h /", "🛠️ find files in … -> run wc") stream into the channel during the turn, grouped by `turn_id`, and the final summary lands in the thread as before. Stored rows verified over the ClickClack REST API (`kind: agent_commentary` / `agent_tool`, shared `turn_id`).

**What was not tested:** DM conversations (the publisher targets `direct_conversation_id`, covered by unit tests, but the live capture is a channel); multi-account setups beyond one account; a ClickClack server predating the activity kinds (degradation there relies on the opt-in default staying off plus best-effort error logging, exercised in unit tests, not live); non-embedded (CLI-backend) agent runtimes.

### Clean-room validation
- Command: `crabbox run --fresh-pr openclaw/openclaw#NNN --preflight --timing-json -- pnpm vitest run extensions/clickclack`
- Provider / lease: pending (filled after PR open)
- Result: pending

### Tests, build, lint
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/clickclack` — 6 files, 32 tests passed (includes 7 new activity-publisher tests + new accounts/http-client/inbound cases)
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — exit 0
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — exit 0
- `pnpm oxlint extensions/clickclack` — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `pnpm config:channels:check` — bundled channel-config metadata in sync (regenerated in this PR for the new `agentActivity` key)
- `pnpm build` — full build passes; the AFTER evidence runs this exact build

## Findings
None open. Two defects were caught and fixed during my own validation pass before posting: (1) the generated bundled channel-config metadata initially wasn't regenerated, which made gateway startup reject `agentActivity` as an unknown key; (2) item events are gated on tool-summary visibility, so the publisher declares channel-owned progress rendering (`suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages: true`) to receive events regardless of session verbose mode, matching the draft-compositor precedent.

## Lineage
None. Consumes the existing `replyOptions.onItemEvent` / `commentaryProgressEnabled` seam already used by the Discord/Telegram/Slack draft paths. The ClickClack server side (activity kinds, `turn_id`, `agent_activity:write` scope) is already merged upstream in the ClickClack repo.

## Remaining risk
Low. The feature is off by default and fully additive; with the flag off the extension behavior is byte-identical to before. With the flag on, publisher failures are logged best-effort and cannot break final delivery (single promise chain isolates transport errors). The main thing to watch is row volume on long multi-tool turns: one row per tool call plus one per commentary segment, PATCH-coalesced within a 700ms debounce window.
